skill.name: runheed
skill.description: Use Runheed to send Node.js and Python errors to a hosted tracker. Review stack traces and incident context through a compatible MCP client.
skill.summary: Review production errors and confirm incident fixes with Runheed.
skill.author: getrunheed

security_audit.summary: Most URL matches are documentation or browser links, and the backticks are Markdown formatting. The skill directs package installation and MCP configuration changes, and its local fallback can expose an agent key. It also proposes hosted production telemetry without a data review step and pairs the demo with a paid plan recommendation.

remediation.issue: Direct package installation and automatic local execution
remediation.suggestion: Publish verifiable packages and document artifact integrity checks. Require explicit approval before installing an SDK, launching the local MCP package, or changing client configuration.

remediation.issue: Agent key requested and passed as a CLI argument
remediation.suggestion: Prefer remote OAuth. For local clients, have users configure a scoped key through a secret store without sharing it in chat or passing it as an argument.

remediation.issue: Production telemetry lacks a data review step
remediation.suggestion: Document which fields leave the application and how they are retained. Require authorized approval and verify redaction in staging before enabling production capture.

remediation.issue: Paid plan promotion is coupled to the demo
remediation.suggestion: Offer checkout links only when asked. Disclose the promotional code and keep commercial recommendations separate from error triage and demo results.

content.value_statement: Copying production stack traces into chat leaves out useful incident context. Runheed makes captured errors available to a compatible coding agent for triage and follow-up.
actual_capabilities: Guide SDK setup for Node.js, TypeScript, and Python applications.
Describe OAuth setup for a compatible remote MCP client.
Review synthetic errors through the Runheed demo when connected.
Inspect captured errors with stack traces and breadcrumbs.
Verify a test event and mark a tracked error resolved after a fix ships.
limitations: Production tracking requires a paid workspace and a configured SDK or ingest integration.
First-party SDKs support Node.js and Python, not automatic browser or mobile capture.
Runheed does not provide performance tracing, session replay, or release health.
Runheed does not automatically create issues in GitHub, Linear, or Jira.

use_cases.title: Evaluate the demo
use_cases.description: Review synthetic incidents in an approved demo connection without sending production data.

use_cases.title: Triage an application error
use_cases.description: Use captured stack traces and breadcrumbs to identify where an error starts and propose a fix.

use_cases.title: Verify a deployed fix
use_cases.description: Review recent occurrences after deployment and confirm whether the tracked error is ready to be marked resolved.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Review a sample error
prompt_templates.scenario: An approved Runheed demo connection is already available.
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize the top sample error. Explain the likely cause, and do not change any settings.

prompt_templates.title: Basic: Plan staging setup
prompt_templates.scenario: A Node.js application needs error tracking in staging.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Runheed setup checklist for staging. Include what to review before installing packages or sending telemetry.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Triage a recent error
prompt_templates.scenario: An authorized Runheed workspace already contains application errors.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the selected recent error and identify the first relevant application frame. Summarize the breadcrumbs and suggest a test without changing incident status.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Check a fix after deployment
prompt_templates.scenario: A fix has shipped and the error is still open.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review recent occurrences of this error since deployment. Report any recurrence and recommend whether to resolve it. Ask for approval before changing its status.

output_examples.input: Summarize the selected error in the Runheed demo.
output_examples.output: The sample request fails while validating a missing field. The last breadcrumb shows the request reached the handler before validation failed.

output_examples.input: Check whether the selected error returned after deployment.
output_examples.output: No new occurrences appear in the reviewed window. That does not rule out a recurrence. The error remains open pending your approval.

best_practices: Confirm the workspace and access scope before reviewing production errors.
Review and redact telemetry in staging before enabling production capture.
Prefer OAuth and keep any fallback key out of chat and command history.
anti_patterns: Installing packages or registering an MCP server without approval.
Sending production error details to a workspace you have not verified.
Marking an error resolved before confirming that the fix shipped.

faq.question: Can I try Runheed before paying?
faq.answer: The skill documents a demo with sample errors and no account requirement. Production tracking requires a paid plan.

faq.question: What application runtimes have SDKs?
faq.answer: The documented first-party SDKs support Node.js and Python. TypeScript applications use the Node.js SDK.

faq.question: How does the agent connect?
faq.answer: A compatible client can connect to the hosted MCP server with OAuth. The documented local fallback requires an agent key.

faq.question: Do I need to share an agent key in chat?
faq.answer: No. Prefer OAuth. For a local integration, configure the key privately through an approved secret store.

faq.question: Does Runheed automatically fix code or file tickets?
faq.answer: No. Runheed provides incident context and resolution status. The coding agent handles code changes, and Runheed does not create external tickets automatically.

faq.question: What should I review before enabling production capture?
faq.answer: Verify the workspace, permissions, telemetry fields, redaction, and retention. Test with non-sensitive data before enabling production capture.
